dishes.name: Bitterballen
dishes.desc: Crisp, deep-fried balls with a molten beef ragout inside, eaten with mustard. The standard bar snack in Amsterdam's brown cafes at borrel hour.

dishes.name: Poffertjes
dishes.desc: Small puffy buckwheat pancakes served hot with butter and icing sugar. A fixture of Amsterdam's street stalls and pancake houses.

dishes.name: Oliebollen
dishes.desc: Deep-fried dough balls with raisins, dusted with sugar. Sold from winter stalls around New Year, and in bakeries much of the year.

dishes.name: Dutch apple pie
dishes.desc: Deep, spiced apple pie with a lattice or crumble top, served with whipped cream. The cafes of the Jordaan made it a signature of the city.

dishes.name: Rijsttafel
dishes.desc: A spread of small Indonesian dishes served around rice, a legacy of colonial ties. Amsterdam has the country's deepest tradition of Indonesian restaurants.
